payload.body:
dc's review of 84f9870 (0088 row 2, second amendment), on a scratch copy. Three parts: an OK on the change, one test gap with the arm that closes it, and one older defect that this change now makes harder to fix.

1. OK on the change. My fb991 probe now reads EOF at 84f9870: a tool started by a built-in no longer gets the terminal. I read your four arms and agree with them. devbin_offer_upgrade runs at bin/devbin top level, outside any gate, so the flag does not touch it.

2. Mutants beyond your five, each on a fresh copy of 84f9870, run against the 0088 arms in runlog.bats and the tty arms in clean.bats:
- `[ -t 0 ]` changed to `[ -t 1 ]` in run_gate: SURVIVES.
- `[ -t 0 ]` changed to `[ -t 2 ]` in run_gate: SURVIVES.
  Both survive because your pty arm puts all three fds on the terminal. The arm below kills both (stdin on a tty, output piped, as in `devbin check | tee`). A no-op control stays green with it, 11 of 11. The tree is locked, so it is yours to land:

    @test "the flag reads the gate's STDIN, not its output: a terminal in, a pipe out, is still a person (0088)" {
      require_pty
      d="$(gate_probe @builtin)"
      run run_tty_eof env PROJECT_ROOT="$d" DEVBIN_NAME=devbin RUN_LINE=@builtin DEVBIN_LIB="$DEVBIN_LIB" \
        bash -c 'bash "$1" 2>&1 | cat' _ "$d/probe.sh"
      assert_output_contains "flag=1"
      assert_output_contains "tool read EOF"
    }

- In clean, dropping the `[ ! -t 0 ] &&` conjunct: SURVIVES, and is equivalent.
- In clean, changing `${DEVBIN_GATE_TTY:-0}` to `:-1`: SURVIVES, and is equivalent.
  clean is reached only through run_builtin_gate, so under the gate its stdin is always /dev/null and the flag is always set. Both terms are dead code. I suggest dropping them, or saying in the comment that they are unreachable, so the next reader does not take them for live guards.
- Setting gate_tty to empty: KILLED by your stale-flag arm.

3. An older defect, and 84f9870 makes it harder to fix. When a person runs `devbin fullcycle` without --force at a terminal, clean refuses "no tty". This is NOT caused by 0088: my pty probe reads the same refusal on 07b661a^, before 0088, while clean run directly asks there. The cause is lib/cmd/fullcycle:461, `done < <(_fullcycle_phases)`: every phase's stdin is the phase list. The comment above the phase case ("NO `< /dev/null` ... would defeat clean's confirmation") has been false for as long as that loop has read its input this way. The consent notice ("clean asks on the tty ... That is the refusal you will meet") is true only because of this defect.
  What 84f9870 adds: the flag is "always set, so an outer gate's value cannot stand". fullcycle is itself gated (:770), so the child clean's gate sees /dev/null and writes 0. Moving the phase list to another fd would no longer be enough. The fix would also need a nested gate to trust its parent's 1 while still ignoring a stale variable. From the environment alone those two look the same. A boundary like DEVBIN_RUN_ID's child inheritance (bin/devbin) is one place to key it. A variable set in a person's own shell is a contrived case; a nested devbin is fullcycle's normal shape.
  My proposal: file this as its own issue (I can write it), and let it not block 0088's close. Whether the "always set" rule gives way to nesting is hv's call, through you.

Probe arms: scratchpad/r0088/arm.bats (the fullcycle arm plus the direct-clean control) and arm-fd.bats. Runner: r0088/mut.sh.

Once your suite at 84f9870 ends green, and once you have decided about the fd arm, I close 0088.
